design:
## Design tests

After the bench, the new wheel and the rules of revision 20 were read blind in whole test scenes among other events (`vision/design_tests_v022.md`, two rounds, eight pictures): a tier-4 street with the square-wheeled bicycle, a jumper and the dropped ice cream; a tier-4 park with the reading walker, a sleeping cat placed after her, the barrow's new wheel and a runner; a garden with the sprinkler and a kick; a garden with the frying pan over a flower bed on the ground and a jumper; a park with the ladder against the hedge; and a tier-4 playground with the reading walker, the bicycle and a sleeping dog. Every rule read as meant but one. The bucket lay "right in her path, so she looks about to trip", the cat "curled up asleep", not linked to her; the barrow's "wheel is drawn as a square, which would be impossible to roll"; the sprinkler's hose came "in from off the left edge"; the pan "looks more like a frying pan or saucepan than a watering can"; the ladder "leans slightly with nothing to lean against". But the two jumpers at the back of the street and the playground, clear of the stall and the fence, were still hedged between jumping and standing with arms raised, while the one at the front of the garden was "jumping in the air". A jumper's lift is drawn to scale, so revision 20 also keeps a jumper in the front half of the ground; rebuilt there, both read as "clearly jumping".
intro: Every v0.21 shortfall that revision 20 and the bench addressed read in full in the nineteenth screen: the jumper as jumping in all three of its pictures, the ladder leaning on nothing as standing by itself in all three, and the redrawn square wheel as square ("its wheel is square, which wouldn't roll"), with no reader seeing a round wheel inside it. No sprinkler hose rose from the bottom edge, no foot stood on a wheelbarrow's handles, and no kick was aimed at anyone. No item of the set was misread, its contradictions are back to 1.00, and 285 of its 287 scored items had full marks (0.997 over all items; 0.989 in v0.21). One template still falls short of the gate: the frying pan, now out of the street, read as a frying pan in two of its three garden probes and as "a grey, round watering can" in the third, held close in front of the flowers with its handle hidden. 63 of 64 templates pass (61 in v0.21). `vision/flaws_v022.md` sends the pan to the isolation bench for v0.23, with the older man's profile head, whose grey ring of hair read as a beard and turned his walk the other way.
screen: Across all 65 pictures 4 of 755 scored items fell short of full marks (6 of 744 in v0.21): two half points in the set, and one misread in the probes, on both of its contradiction items. The two half points are both in the tier-4 street, from the same reader, each an inference offered as one of two readings: a dog with a paw raised in front of a man eating ice cream on a bench, "perhaps hoping for some ... or just walking by", and a reading walker whose box lay "to the side of / slightly ahead of" her, who "might trip over it, or ... might simply walk past it". In the probes, the frying pan held close in front of a flower bed was "a grey, round watering can ... a watering can, a bucket or even a stone" ("I saw nothing that looks impossible"). Two scorers gave no half point at all and listed eight and nine hedged items they credited in full. Unintended oddities were 25 in the set (24 in v0.21) and rose in the probes from 34 to 54, most of them small remarks on drawing. What the readers noticed: the older man's grey ring of hair, seen in profile, as a beard or a face mask, so that the way he faced was unclear (four probes) and, in the tier-4 park, he seemed to walk toward the sleeping cat behind him ("he might trip over it or step on it"); a runner and a woman with a pram heading toward each other in the tier-2 playground; a duck close to an angler's float that "might go for the bait" (two probes); a wheelbarrow's stand "like a boot" (two probes); hoses' bulges and bends; and the older ones (goats, wind under a clear sky, a stall with nobody at it).
redrawn: The three v0.21 failures and the square wheel all read in full except the frying pan: the jumper at 1.00 over three pictures (0.833 in v0.21), the ladder leaning on nothing at 1.00 over nine items (0.889), and the square wheel at 1.00 over nine (0.967), in its new drawing in one probe and on the bicycle in two set pictures. The frying pan stayed at 0.778: out of the street, it was misread once in a garden instead. Of the templates whose placement revision 20 changed, the runner, the kick and the sprinkler read in full; the reading walker took one half point in the tier-4 street, where her box lay a little to the side of her line (0.958 over 12 items).
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (54 in three, 6 in four, 1 in five, 3 in six), and 63 of 64 pass. The one that falls short is the frying pan, for the second screen running, both times with its handle hard to see: held up face-on at a raised planter in the v0.21 street, and held close in front of the flowers in a v0.22 garden probe. The street rule removed one cause; the drawing itself goes to the bench in v0.23. About five templates of the gate's movement between screens is reader variance (the v0.9 retest).
inspection: Building and inspecting the set and the probes found one more thing, fixed before the screen. In a garden probe a begging dog stood 40 px in front of a sprinkler's hose, and the hose was drawn running under its body, as if the dog stood on it; the sprinkler's hose now keeps clear of the legs of anyone just in front of it, not only of their feet. The two other pictures with a sprinkler, one of them in the set, rebuild exactly under the new rule; the probe could not be placed again in a garden in eight seeds, and was rebuilt in the park with the same three templates. The tier-4 street was the hardest cell to place under revision 20: it came on the 11th seed of a second search, after the showcase seed and 32 other seeds of up to 40 casts each had failed.
calib: The sprinkler's cue salience moved by +0.27 (its hose now off a side edge), the ladder's by -0.15 (its top against the hedge; measured in 3 scenes) and the frying pan's by +0.11 (measured in 9 scenes, none in the street); every other template's by at most 0.01.
